dish: Coconut rice with Lombok-style grilled ayam taliwang & sambal
address: Ci Yuan Hawker Centre, 51 Hougang Avenue 9, #01-40, Singapore 538776
w: A MICHELIN Guide-listed stall that pairs fragrant coconut rice with Ayam Taliwang, the fiery Lombok-style grilled chicken — the smoky, chilli-slicked bird against the cool creamy rice. The Ci Yuan branch of a beloved north-east name, right in Hougang.

dish: Teochew braised duck on yam rice with dark braising sauce
address: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-01, Singapore 530105
w: One of Singapore's best Teochew braised duck rice stalls, tucked in Hougang's Hainanese Village Centre (Lorong Ah Soo). Tender lean duck over yam rice, drenched in a mildly sweet-savoury five-spice sauce, with an anchovy-loaded sambal. Opens at dawn and usually sells out by early lunch.

dish: Wet-style fried Hokkien prawn mee, same recipe since 1960
address: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, 209 Hougang Street 21, #01-66, Singapore 530209
w: Third- and fourth-generation hawkers who have fried their wet-style Hokkien mee to the same recipe since 1960 — whole prawns, squid rings and pork belly over noodles and bee hoon fried dry so they drink up a prawn-head-and-pork-rib stock, with free-flow crispy lard. Named for its old Simon Road home, now relocated to Kovan 209.

dish: Clean sliced-&-fried fish soup, the 'hei bai' combo with milk
w: Widely cited as Singapore's best-rated fish soup — a clean, refined broth from a couple who started at Zion Road Blk 91 in 2002 before landing under a quiet Hougang coffeeshop. The 'hei bai' bowl of fried and sliced fish together, done with milk, is the order.

dish: Lard-fried oyster omelette with big oysters & fried kway teow
n: Hougang Oyster Omelette & Fried Kway Teow
w: A 30-year Hougang heritage stall run by Mr and Mrs Ong that still fries its oyster omelette in pork lard, with big juicy oysters and a fragrant char kway teow alongside. One of the island's best-rated orh luak, worth the queue.

dish: Wok-hei Hokkien prawn noodles by an ex-economic-rice cook
address: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, 209 Hougang Street 21, #01-37, Singapore 530209
w: A Kovan 209 Hokkien mee stall run by the former cook of Teow Heng Cooked Food. A big plate of thick and thin noodles with prawns, cuttlefish and pork lard in a seafood broth, fried with wok hei to spare — the 'Davis Prawn Noodles' are the house signature.

dish: Handmade Teochew soon kueh, png kueh & gu chye kueh
w: A roadside Upper Serangoon stall within walking distance of Kovan MRT, packed each morning for handmade Teochew kueh — soon kueh, png kueh — bursting with well-seasoned fillings and made fresh daily.

dish: Award-winning gelato in adventurous local-inspired flavours
w: An under-HDB dessert cafe by an Italy-trained gelato-maker who won the Singapore Gelato Championship in 2019 ('Singapore's Best Gelato') with a Pear, Ginger and Ginger Flower scoop inspired by his father's Chinese rojak. The Hougang outlet opened January 2023.

dish: Made-from-scratch Hokkien prawn mee & char kway teow
address: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-37, Singapore 530105
w: A hidden gem at Hainanese Village Centre serving just two dishes — fried Hokkien prawn mee and char kway teow — with almost everything made from scratch: the prawn stock, pork lard, chilli, even hand-peeled garlic. Run by Mrs Lu and her husband for over a decade.

dish: Chinese-style nasi lemak with crispy fried fish fillet
address: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-30, Singapore 530105
w: The First Class Fragrance nasi lemak — by queue, the most popular stall in the whole of Hainanese Village Centre. Fragrant coconut rice with crispy fried fish fillet, ikan selar, whitebait and sambal for a few dollars; regularly sold out before its stated noon close.

dish: Some of the thinnest, crispiest plain prata in Singapore
w: A 24-hour Indian-Muslim restaurant open since 2008 whose plain prata is repeatedly named among the thinnest and crispiest in Singapore, alongside curries and tandoori. A Hougang prata institution.

dish: Old-school hawker Western: crispy chicken cutlet & grills
address: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-32, Singapore 530105
w: A 30-year hawker Western stall at Hainanese Village Centre — crispy-outside, tender-inside chicken cutlet, chicken chop, pork chop and fish & chips. Old-school flame-grilled plates at hawker prices.

dish: Heartland tachinomiya standing-bar Japanese street food
w: Billed as Singapore's first heartland izakaya — a 'standing bar' under an HDB block in Kovan serving good Japanese street food late into the night (till 2am on Saturdays). A neighbourhood spot for a late plate and a drink.

dish: Soulful lor mee with a secret-ingredient thick gravy
n: Lorong Ah Soo Lor Mee (Fu Yuan Mei Shi)
address: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-36, Singapore 530105
w: A long-loved Hainanese Village Centre stall drawing crowds for its lor mee — flat noodles under a luscious thick gravy with a secret ingredient — and laksa. A Hougang breakfast-crowd fixture.

dish: IG-famous handmade min jiang kueh with generous fillings
w: A humble coffeeshop stall turning out old-school min jiang kueh (Chinese pancakes) far bigger and more generously stuffed than most — red bean, yam, black sesame, matcha, peanut, chocolate — at S$1.30-1.60 a piece. Instagram-famous, and sells out.

dish: Viral crookies, Fatcarons & durian/mochi artisanal cakes
w: A Hougang dessert bakery known for inventive sweets — Korean-French Fatcarons (fat macarons), viral cookie-croissants, mochi cakes and durian cakes. A modern sugar stop in the heartland.

dish: Legit Korean fried chicken with honey butter, from a Korean-run stall
address: Ci Yuan Hawker Centre, 51 Hougang Avenue 9, #01-18, Singapore 538776
w: A Korean-owned hawker stall at Ci Yuan turning out legit Korean fried chicken — crackly-crisp, in flavours like honey butter — from around S$6.50. Hawker-priced KFC done properly.

dish: All-day cafe breakfasts from a Kovan kopitiam, from S$3.90
w: A corner-kopitiam stall two minutes from Kovan MRT doing all-day Western breakfasts — big brekkies, pancakes, creamy scrambled eggs — at hawker prices from S$3.90. Cafe brunch without the cafe markup.

dish: Premium Sangenton pork loin tonkatsu, breaded to order
address: myVillage @ Serangoon Garden, 1 Maju Avenue, #02-07/8/9, Singapore 556679
w: A tonkatsu specialist at myVillage by Chef Tan, using Sangenton pork air-flown from Japan, each loin tenderised and breaded only on order for a super-crunchy cutlet. Serangoon Gardens' go-to for premium katsu and ramen.

dish: Fried Hokkien prawn mee with prawn, pork & abalone
n: Yi Ji Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee
address: 965 Upper Serangoon Road (Mee Sek Food Court), Singapore 534721
w: A popular Kovan fried Hokkien prawn mee that has spawned several branches — a spicy, prawn-rich plate with meat and abalone. The Upper Serangoon original anchors the group.

dish: Giant-portion old-school Western: chicken chop, mixed grill
w: A near-20-year Hougang coffeeshop Western stall famous for huge portions at small prices — chicken chop, sirloin, black-pepper lamb, hot-plate mixed grill and fish & chips. Value old-school hawker Western.

dish: Handmade HK dim sum — prawn dumplings & salted-egg custard bao
n: Yi Dian Xin Hong Kong Dim Sum
w: An affordable Upper Serangoon dim sum spot near Kovan doing hearty Hong Kong-style plates — signature prawn dumplings and salted-egg custard bao among them. A neighbourhood dim sum fix.

dish: Pojangmacha-style Korean tent-bar food & fried chicken
w: A pojangmacha-style Korean tent-bar in Kovan — Korean fried chicken, army stew and soju into the small hours. A late-night Korean option on Upper Serangoon Road.

dish: Super-cheap zhap cai png (economic rice) from S$2
w: A long-running Hougang cai png shop beloved for very affordable economic rice — fried chicken wings, braised pork, stir-fried veg — from as little as S$2 a plate.

dish: Hakka yong tau foo with house-marinated fish paste
n: Mei Xi Hakka Yong Tau Foo
address: Ci Yuan Hawker Centre, 51 Hougang Avenue 9, #01-17, Singapore 538776
w: A Ci Yuan stall where the Hakka owner marinates her own fish paste and offers unusual items — fried bean rolls, deep-fried yam strings and egg rolls — alongside the usual yong tau foo pieces.

dish: All-day brunch, egg dishes & desserts in Serangoon Gardens
w: A Serangoon Gardens brunch cafe (second outlet after Toa Payoh) celebrated for its egg dishes, mains and desserts in an easy neighbourhood setting.

dish: Huge rosti with XL pork chops & chargrilled chicken chop
w: A Western coffeeshop stall hidden in a Kovan kopitiam eight minutes from the MRT, doing generous rosti with oversized pork chops and chargrilled chicken chops at affordable prices.

dish: DIY grill-it-yourself yakiniku with wagyu cuts from S$4.90
address: myVillage @ Serangoon Garden, 1 Maju Avenue, #02-10/11, Singapore 556679
w: The first yakiniku outlet from the Waa Cow! beef-bowl brand — a grill-it-yourself concept at myVillage with cuts like karubi, oyster blade, striploin and ox tongue plus pork, chicken and veg, from S$4.90.

dish: Premium Japanese matcha drinks & matcha Basque cheesecake
w: A Simon Road matcha-specialty cafe near Kovan by the team behind Fat Cat Ice Cream Bar — premium Japanese matcha, creative tea drinks, artisan ice cream and a matcha Basque burnt cheesecake that often sells out within hours.

dish: Fluffy, moist Cantonese-style scrambled egg rice
w: A cult scrambled-egg-rice stall (高文滑蛋饭) — silky wat-dan-style egg over rice — that outgrew its old Kovan 209 home and relocated to a Hougang Avenue 7 coffeeshop in mid-2024.

dish: Freshly fried finger-sized fried carrot cake sticks
address: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-04, Singapore 530105
w: A 40-year-old Hainanese Village Centre stall, now run by second-gen hawker Nicholas Neo, famous for finger-sized fried carrot cake sticks — crisp outside, tender inside — sold by the thousand daily.

dish: Nasi lemak topped with crispy-skinned roasted pork belly
address: Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-28, Singapore 530105
w: A Hainanese Village Centre stall (easy to spot by its fuchsia signboard) plating fragrant coconut rice with crackly-skinned roasted pork belly and crispy ikan bilis — S$3 sets that draw an early crowd.

dish: $1 old-school pandan & kaya sponge cakes and pastries
w: A family-run old-school bakery in Hougang turning out traditional S$1 cakes and pastries — pandan, kaya, sugar rolls — the kind of heartland bakery that's getting rarer.
